chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Accept the invitation for the wedding feast and the circumcision, and do not accept the invitation for the lowering (or circumcising) of the female slaves.

key_terms.خَفْض: Lowering or cutting (referring to female circumcision)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on accepting invitations to wedding and circumcision feasts?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi distinguishes between obligatory social reciprocity and discretionary participation, commanding acceptance for major life-cycle events like weddings and circumcision while advising against attending gatherings for the circumcision of female slaves (khaf al-jawiyat). Shia scholars interpret this as a nuanced guidance on maintaining social bonds while avoiding unnecessary exposure to specific social contexts or potential impropriety associated with the latter event.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Answer (to an invitation for a meal) regarding the wedding feast, and the circumcision, and do not answer regarding the female circumcision’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Accept an invitation for a wedding and circumcision; but do not accept for Khafd (lowering) girls.’”
